# Fractal Scaling API v0.1
Progressive, reversible scaler for finite vector data. Pay-per-request via x402 USDC on Base.

## What it does
POST /scale selects a deterministic progressive subset of input data points at a given scale value
in [0, 1]. Increasing scale always returns a superset of the previous selection. Reversible: decreasing
scale returns the identical smaller set as before.

## Primary endpoint (paid)

POST /scale — 0.02 USDC per successful request

Input:
- points: 2D array of numeric data points [[x1,y1,...], [x2,y2,...], ...] (non-empty, all finite)
- value: float in [0.0, 1.0] — 0 selects 0 points, 1 selects all n points
- weights: optional list of non-negative floats per point (length must equal n)
- weight_floor: float in (0, 1], default 0.15 — minimum weight modifier
- beta: float >= 0, default 1.0 — weight exponent

Output:
- selected_indices: list of integer indices into the input points array
- stats.scale, stats.selected, stats.total, stats.reuse_from_previous,
  stats.mean_coverage_distance, stats.weighted_mean_coverage_distance, stats.max_coverage_distance

If you receive HTTP 402 Payment Required:
1. Read the x402Version=2 payment requirements in the response body.
2. Pay using a compatible x402 client (USDC on Base, eip155:8453).
3. Retry the same request with the payment in the X-PAYMENT or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header.

## Free endpoints
GET /health — health check
GET /.well-known/x402.json — x402 endpoint discovery
GET /ai-agent-policy.json — agent policy

## Key properties
- Deterministic: same points + value always returns the same selection
- Progressive: scale(0.6) is always a superset of scale(0.4) for the same dataset
- Reversible: returning to a prior scale returns identical indices
- No state mutation: stats() does not mutate scaler state

## Payment details
- Network: Base (eip155:8453)
- Asset: USDC (0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913)
- Recipient: 0x60c402878EfcEcAe5733A88075328Aa2320C39BE
- Price: 0.02 USDC per successful /scale request
- Protocol: x402 v2 (scheme: exact)
